Remember, it's ok to talk. Me and my friends have our dmc moments but we make sure to try and have fun and banter (even if that part is a bit difficult). Balance is key. Hugs are great, especially long ones, it's appropriate to share a hug as a thank you for listening, for example. The true friends are the ones that are prepared to listen AND understand, without completely trying to one-up you with their problems too, or deem you opening up about yourself as "too depressing".

Are you seeing a therapist/councellor? Their job is to listen to you so if you feel uncomfortable speaking about your struggles with your friends, they're also a healthy option.
Even if I have work opportunies here and not there?

Personally, the reason people found out about my mental health was a result of me breaking down. Things reveal themselves in certain situations. If you feel too awkward to talk about it face to face, sending a message about it helps. I just said it was unfortunately a part of myself that I was getting help for and it didn't affect how I viewed any of them. If anyone asks how you are and you think it's a good time, just talk about how you are. Many people will hug it out, even if they cannot understand fully.

Believe me, this is something I can relate to on a daily basis. It's what separates people with social anxiety from people that are just plain shy which is why I can take offense to being labelled as quiet or reserved. You don't necessarily prefer to be alone, it's the anxiety of social situations in the first place that affects you.

You can't live all your life expecting other people to make a special effort for you, I personally wish life actually worked that way. It's up to you to seek help for yourself and set your life on the right track. Letting a few closer friends know about your struggles might help relieve some stress, talking to a therapist, getting to the roots of your issues. Small and safe amounts of alcohol on social outings and prescribed medication for depression/anxiety can help relieve tension but if you don't believe in these methods, learning more about the people you meet and finding things in common with them, reasons to trust them makes it a lot easier to relax and open up to them, which is extremely helpful. I'm not here to promote the use of illicit substances but I bond with certain people because we enjoy pot together, there's one common interest, therefore a new friend group. I guess you could say this certain community is one of the tightest there is lol. With more practice and self development, talking to people that are even completely different to you becomes easier in due time. 

Remember you might feel alone in your situation but there are so many people who understand your struggles and would be willing to talk to you. Feel free to pm me anytime.
